findings.title: labels= silently dropped (partially or entirely) in animations whenever frame_rate*duration < sample count
findings.description: The labels= docstring promises: 'in an ANIMATION, per-point labels are drawn once and remain visible in every frame', and label_alpha='s docstring says labels 'persist across every frame on both backends'. On the matplotlib backend this is only true when the animation frame count (frame_rate*duration) exceeds the per-dataset sample count. Animations INTERPOLATE (or here, DOWNSAMPLE) each trajectory to frame_rate*duration points, then _expand_labels() (hypertools/plot/plot.py:3291-3304) remaps labels onto the new indices with an unconditional `expanded[j] = lab` -- when several original indices collapse onto one new index, later None labels OVERWRITE earlier real labels. Measured: 30 samples, 2 labels -> duration=1,frame_rate=5 (5 frames): 0 labels survive; duration=1,frame_rate=20 (20 frames): 1 of 2 survives; defaults (900 frames): both survive. No warning is emitted; the labels just vanish from the rendered animation (verified at the artist level: labels_and_points global len 0, zero Annotation children, and visually in the saved gif). Short animations of longer recordings (e.g. duration=5s of a 300-sample EEG trace at 30fps = 150 frames) are entirely reasonable scientist use.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
from hypertools.plot import matplotlib_backend as mb
A = np.cumsum(np.random.RandomState(50).randn(30,5), axis=0)
labels = [None]*30; labels[0], labels[15] = 'L0', 'L15'
fig, ani = hyp.plot(A, animate=True, duration=1.0, frame_rate=5, labels=labels, show=False)
print(len(mb.labels_and_points))  # 0 -- both labels silently gone
findings.expected: Both labels drawn once and visible across frames (docstring), or at minimum a UserWarning that labels were dropped.
findings.actual: labels_and_points exists: True | len: 0; returned fig annotations: [] -- and with frame_rate=20: len 1 (one label silently lost). Unit-level: _expand_labels(labels,[30],[5]) -> non-None labels=[]

findings.title: elev= and azim= are accepted, fully functional camera kwargs but have NO entry in the plot() docstring
findings.description: plot() has elev=10, azim=-60 in its signature; both are threaded to the matplotlib backend (ax.view_init) and the plotly backend (scene.camera.eye) and verifiably change the rendered image (pixel hashes differ; plotly camera eye moves from (0.96,-1.66,0.34) to (0,0,1.95) for elev=90,azim=0), and they are also forwarded to plot_stream(). The 1000-line docstring documents every other signature parameter but has no 'elev :' or 'azim :' entry anywhere (grep over the docstring body returns nothing). Users cannot discover the camera-angle controls from help(hyp.plot).
findings.repro:
python - <<'EOF'
import inspect, hypertools as hyp
src = inspect.getdoc(hyp.plot)
print('elev' in src, 'azim :' in src)  # False False
EOF
findings.expected: Documented parameter entries for elev/azim (camera elevation/azimuth in degrees, defaults 10/-60, both backends).
findings.actual: grep of docstring lines 210-1224 for '^    elev'/'^    azim' -> no matches; runtime behavior verified working: default (elev,azim)=(10, -60); custom -> (90, 0); pixels differ (aae3d209 vs 17cb34b9)

findings.title: fmt list length is never validated: too short crashes with bare IndexError, too long is silently ignored
findings.description: GH #206 added clean length validation for every per-dataset list kwarg (color/colors, marker/markers, linestyle/linestyles: 'X= was given as a list/tuple of length N, but there are M dataset(s)...'), but fmt -- also documented as 'str or list of strings' -- was left out (plot.py:2508-2514 assigns `draw_fmt = fmt` verbatim). A 1-entry fmt list against 2 datasets raises `IndexError: list index out of range` at plot.py:2333 (`has_line_component(fmt[idx])`) with no mention of fmt=; a 3-entry list against 2 datasets silently drops the extra entry with no warning. Inconsistent with its sibling kwargs' polished errors.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp

findings.title: A single RGB(A) tuple as color= is always misinterpreted as a per-dataset list (rejected or split into float 'colors')
findings.description: matplotlib users routinely pass color=(r,g,b). plot()'s GH #206 broadcast treats ANY tuple/list as one-entry-per-dataset: with 1 or 2 datasets, color=(0.2,0.4,0.6) raises 'color= was given as a list/tuple of length 3, but there are 1 dataset(s) to plot; pass either a single value...' -- actively misleading, since the user DID pass a single (tuple) value; with exactly 3 datasets it is silently split into per-dataset floats and dies deep in matplotlib ('0.9 is not a valid value for color...'). The workaround (wrap in a list: color=[(r,g,b)]*n) works and the docstring only promises 'str or list of str', but the same release deliberately solved this exact tuple-vs-list ambiguity for **kwargs extras (dashes=(4,2) is applied verbatim -- see the **kwargs docstring rationale), so the dedicated color= kwarg failing on it is an avoidable trap. Suggest detecting a 3/4-length all-numeric tuple as a single color (as matplotlib does) or naming the wrap-in-a-list fix in the error.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
A = np.cumsum(np.random.RandomState(1).randn(30,5),axis=0)
hyp.plot(A, color=(0.2,0.4,0.6), show=False)  # ValueError length 3 vs 1 dataset
B,C = A+1, A+2
hyp.plot([A,B,C], color=(0.9,0.4,0.1), show=False)  # ValueError: 0.9 is not a valid value for color
findings.expected: A bare RGB(A) tuple treated as one color broadcast to every dataset, or an error that names the list-wrapping workaround.
findings.actual: ValueError: color= was given as a list/tuple of length 3, but there are 1 dataset(s) to plot; pass either a single value (broadcast to every dataset) or a list/tuple of length 1.  |  3 datasets: ValueError: 0.9 is not a valid value for color: supported inputs are (r, g, b) and (r, g, b, a) 0-1 float tuples; ...

findings.title: zlabel= text collides with the legend on matplotlib 3-D plots (both occupy the right margin)
findings.description: On the matplotlib backend, Axes3D places the z-axis label at the RIGHT edge of the axes -- exactly where hypertools puts the legend. With zlabel= and any legend (legend=/names=) together, the zlabel text renders on top of the legend box (w1 evidence: 'PC3' sits directly over the 'subject 1' legend entry and its line sample strikes through the text). Each feature alone renders fine (isolation PNGs); _fit_right_legend() widens the figure for the legend but does not account for the z-axis label. The plotly backend has no such collision (it puts the z title on the left).
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
d = lambda s: np.cumsum(np.random.RandomState(s).randn(60,8),axis=0)
hyp.plot([d(1), d(2)], names=['subject 1','subject 2'], xlabel='PC1', ylabel='PC2', zlabel='PC3', save_path='collide.png', show=False)
findings.expected: zlabel and legend both readable without overlapping text.
findings.actual: Rendered PNG shows 'PC3' overlapping the legend's first entry (see w1_neuro_names_title_axes.png, right edge ~y=235-275); zlabel-only and legend-only control images have no overlap.

In 1.0 plot() returns ONLY a Figure (or HyperAnimation / return_model dict) -- the code comment at plot.py:2720 ('Return shape (Jeremy decision #2)') and the Returns section both say so, and runtime confirms type(fig)=Figure with no (fig, ax, data) tuple. Stale 0.x wording contradicting the Returns section of the same docstring.

findings.title: names= accepts a bare string and silently splits it into characters
findings.description: names= runs `names = list(names)` (plot.py:2264) before the length check, so names='ab' with 2 datasets silently becomes legend entries 'a' and 'b' -- no error, no warning (verified: legend ['a','b']). With a mismatched-length string the error reports the character count ('got 3' for names='abc' with 2 datasets), which is confusing. A scalar string should be rejected ('names= must be a list with one entry per dataset') or wrapped.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
A = np.cumsum(np.random.RandomState(1).randn(30,5),axis=0); B = A+1
fig = hyp.plot([A,B], names='ab', show=False)
print([t.get_text() for t in fig.axes[0].get_legend().get_texts()])  # ['a','b']
findings.expected: TypeError/ValueError explaining names= takes a list of per-dataset names.
findings.actual: names='ab' (bare str, 2 datasets) -> legend ['a', 'b'] (silently split into chars)

findings.title: legend= accepts a bare string (undocumented) and broadcasts it into N identical legend entries
findings.description: legend='s docstring says 'list or bool', but a bare string is accepted and broadcast by parse_kwargs to every dataset, producing duplicate legend entries: hyp.plot([A,B], legend='groups') renders a legend containing 'groups' twice (once per trace color; visually confirmed). Either reject scalar strings, treat one as a shared single entry, or document the broadcast. Related: a wrong-length legend LIST correctly raises, but the message names 'label=' (the internal mpl kwarg) rather than 'legend=': "label= was given as a list/tuple of length 1, but there are 2 dataset(s)...".
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
A = np.cumsum(np.random.RandomState(1).randn(30,5),axis=0); B = A+1
fig = hyp.plot([A,B], legend='groups', show=False)
print([t.get_text() for t in fig.axes[0].get_legend().get_texts()])  # ['groups','groups']
findings.expected: Error, deduplication, or documented behavior for a scalar-string legend; wrong-length error should say legend= not label=.
findings.actual: legend='groups' -> legend entries ['groups', 'groups'] ; wrong length -> ValueError: label= was given as a list/tuple of length 1, but there are 2 dataset(s) to plot; ...

findings.title: labels= length mismatch is silently accepted despite docstring 'Must be dimensionality of data (x)'
findings.description: labels= with 1 entry for 30 points annotates only the first point; 50 entries for 30 points silently drops the extra 20 -- no error or warning either way. The docstring says the list 'Must be dimensionality of data', and the sibling per-observation kwarg hue= DOES validate strictly ('hue has N entries but the data has M observations'). Off-by-N label lists (e.g. after dropping rows) will silently annotate the wrong points.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
A = np.cumsum(np.random.RandomState(1).randn(30,5),axis=0)
hyp.plot(A, labels=['only-one-label'], show=False)  # no error, 1 annotation
hyp.plot(A, labels=['L%d'%i for i in range(50)], show=False)  # no error, 30 annotations
findings.expected: ValueError mirroring hue='s: 'labels has 1 entry but the data has 30 observations...'
findings.actual: labels len 1 vs 30 points: NO error; 1 annotations drawn: ['only-one-label'] | labels len 50 vs 30 points: NO error; 30 annotations drawn

findings.title: size= is not validated up front: malformed values crash after the full pipeline with errors that never name size=
findings.description: size='big' -> 'ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2)'; size=[8] -> 'ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 2, got 1)' -- both raised from matplotlib's Figure.set_size_inches at the END of _draw (matplotlib_backend.py:2176), i.e. AFTER the expensive reduce/align pipeline already ran, and neither message mentions size=. Contrast with label_alpha=/colorbar=/resample=, which all fail fast with named messages before the pipeline. (size=[-5,5] at least gets matplotlib's own decent 'figure size must be positive finite not [-5 5]'. A (w,h) tuple works fine although the docstring says 'list'.)
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
A = np.cumsum(np.random.RandomState(1).randn(30,5),axis=0)
hyp.plot(A, size='big', show=False)   # ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2)
hyp.plot(A, size=[8], show=False)     # ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 2, got 1)
findings.expected: Fail-fast ValueError naming size= ('size= must be a [width, height] pair in inches; got ...') before the pipeline runs.
findings.actual: ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2)  /  ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 2, got 1)  (from matplotlib figure.py:3139 via matplotlib_backend.py:2176 fig.set_size_inches(size))

findings.title: explore= (and animation dimensionality) misuse raises AssertionError instead of ValueError
findings.description: explore=True with 2-D data raises `AssertionError: Explore mode is currently only supported for 3D plots.` (bare assert at plot.py:2362-2364). Similarly the animation dimensionality guard (matplotlib_backend.py:~1996) is an assert. Asserts are stripped under `python -O` (silently skipping validation) and AssertionError is the wrong exception type for user input -- every comparable guard in plot() raises ValueError with a fix hint.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
A = np.cumsum(np.random.RandomState(1).randn(30,5),axis=0)
hyp.plot(A, ndims=2, explore=True, show=False)
findings.expected: ValueError('explore=True is only supported for 3-D static plots; pass ndims=3 ...').
findings.actual: AssertionError: Explore mode is currently only supported for 3D plots.

findings.title: Non-numeric elev=/azim= accepted silently; crash deferred to draw/save time with a cryptic numpy error
findings.description: hyp.plot(A, elev='up', show=False) returns a 'valid' Figure; the failure only surfaces when the figure is drawn/saved: 'TypeError: ufunc deg2rad not supported for the input types...' from deep inside mpl_toolkits -- never naming elev=. Since every other scalar kwarg with constraints (label_alpha, focused, duration, frame_rate) is validated fail-fast, elev/azim should be too (they are also the two undocumented kwargs -- see finding 002).
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
A = np.cumsum(np.random.RandomState(1).randn(30,5),axis=0)
fig = hyp.plot(A, elev='up', show=False)  # no error here
fig.savefig('/tmp/x.png')  # TypeError: ufunc 'deg2rad' not supported...
findings.expected: Fail-fast ValueError naming elev=/azim= as numbers in degrees.
findings.actual: plot() succeeds; savefig raises: TypeError: ufunc 'deg2rad' not supported for the input types, and the inputs could not be safely coerced to any supported types according to the casting rule ''safe''

findings.title: ax= given a non-Axes object fails with cryptic AttributeError ('str' object has no attribute 'name')
findings.description: plot.py:1560-1565 touches ax.name to check 3-D-ness without first checking the object is an Axes: hyp.plot(A, ax='not-an-axes') raises `AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'name'` -- no mention of ax=. A one-line isinstance check would give a named TypeError.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
A = np.cumsum(np.random.RandomState(1).randn(30,5),axis=0)

findings.title: plot() docstring has no Examples section (and its 'Geo' input mention is a 0.x leftover)
findings.description: The flagship API function's ~1000-line docstring contains zero runnable examples (grep 'Examples' -> no match), so this audit's 'run every docstring example verbatim' step had only the inline fragments to execute (the manip= pipeline example, the names= example, the nested-hue form, the animate= dict form -- all executed and all pass). Numpydoc convention for a function this central is an Examples section. Also the x= description ('Numpy array, DataFrame, String, Geo or mixed list') still advertises 'Geo' objects, which 1.0's public API never hands to users (DataGeometry is documented internally as an unpickle-only legacy shell; hyp.load returns raw data) -- untestable as a user input without private construction.
findings.repro: python -c "import inspect, hypertools as hyp; d=inspect.getdoc(hyp.plot); print('Examples' in d, 'Geo' in d)"  # False True
findings.expected: An Examples section with 2-3 copy-pasteable calls; x= description matching 1.0's actual accepted inputs.
findings.actual: 'Examples' absent from the docstring; 'Geo' present in the x= description.
